tools.name: add_managed_runtime_server
tools.title: Add one managed Node through native provider control
tools.description: Creates or resumes one deterministic Add-Server job for the exact owned StackKit deployment. The standard `Idempotency-Key` is mandatory. Replaying the same key with the same canonical request returns the original job, lease, runtime-server, resource-generation, and provider-operation correlations; reusing it with different intent fails with 409. The raw key is never persisted or returned. A lost response or an uncertain native-admission outcome remains resumable only with the same key. HTTP acceptance means native admission is durable and provider reconciliation is pending; it never claims that the VM is already provisioned or healthy. Fresh admission atomically reserves the authenticated tenant/owner capacity slot with the lease generation and provider operation. When authoritative native admission finds that bounded capacity full, it persists a non-retryable 403 outcome and replaying that denied job returns the same outcome. Exact replays of an already committed admission reuse its existing reservation. This version has no automatic reservation release: terminal or local decommission state alone does not free a slot. Lease inventory and feature-delivery flags never authorize or deny capacity. Hosted fresh admission also requires the v2-signed commercial runtime and provider entitlements plus the signed `cloud.runtime.credits` `managed_servers` mode/limit decision; feature flags alone never grant provider capacity. Self-host OSS uses its construction-fixed static release-manifest policy instead of a SaaS entitlement dependency.

tools.description: Authenticated, idempotent recovery for a persisted `waiting_enrollment`, `waiting_provider_provision`, or `waiting_canonical_guard` job whose `next_resume_at` has been overdue beyond the bounded grace period. The server validates the owned StackKit deployment, source job, wait reason, exact lease, active foundation role, and canonical Node as one operation. It atomically retires the exact source wait, creates or rehydrates one deterministic replacement deploy bound to the same lease and Node, and replays that job on later calls. Before handler entry, queue workers atomically acquire the durable `tenant/stack` compatibility execution claim; this serializes different jobs for the same StackKit deployment across Techstack replicas. The claim remains durable `running` until the handler exits, including during cancellation. This endpoint never invokes provider VM creation or selects a newer VM. A replacement found durable `running` after a crash remains fail-closed, is reported as the same job, and is never duplicated automatically; runtime-action reconciliation remains a separate operator concern.

tools.name: run_server_maintenance_action
tools.title: Queue an owned server OS update plan, OS update or reboot
tools.description: Requires the Edge-signed `techstack.servers.maintenance` entitlement, ownership of the server in the tenant, and current server-bound standing authority for delegated native MCP calls. These three ordinary actions require no fresh MFA or separate owner_approved assertion. Reboot and os_update require expected_impact_digest from the preview the user confirmed. Impact is compared atomically at admission and again at execution claim; changed or incomplete evidence sends no command and requires a refreshed preview and renewed confirmation with a new request key. The body is decoded strictly: exact lowercase keys, no duplicates, no unknown fields. A replay with the same Idempotency-Key returns the stored receipt before target validation. One reboot or OS update and, separately, one update plan may be active per server; a job not finished by its deadline fails with `deadline_exceeded` and frees its slot. The action is offered in `allowed_actions` only when the server agent advertises `stackkit.host-maintenance.v1`, and `reboot` only when the server also reports `host_boot_id`. Refusals are client-error-envelope/v1 documents; 409 `reason_code` is one of control_plane_host, substrate_node, protected_demo_server, service_locked, maintenance_active, node_operation_active, plan_stale, agent_capability_missing, boot_id_unknown, agent_not_connected, heartbeat_stale, inventory_revision_stale, idempotency_key_reused, impact_confirmation_required, impact_changed or impact_unavailable; 403 carries entitlement_required or maintenance_origin_authority_denied.

expected_plan_digest.description: os_update only: the plan_digest of a completed os_update_plan for this server that is at most 15 minutes old.

owner_approved.description: Optional legacy field; it does not grant maintenance authority.

tools.name: run_stackkit_operation
tools.title: Run an admitted StackKit operation
tools.description: Uses the same tenant- and owner-scoped dispatcher as the operator UI. The node executes through its authenticated channel, current release pin, native Advanced catalog and issued operation capability. Techstack never executes Terramate, apply, rollback, backup or restore itself. A mutation requires owner_approved; service locks and active server maintenance are checked before enqueue. Direct backup_run and backup_configure remain Basement-only; managed kits keep their schedule and sealed target-renewal authority. backup_configure derives the node's target and plan from existing custody and accepts no credential fields. advanced_change_set requires candidate_spec; rollback requires an exact rollback_target_ref; restore_drill may reuse a snapshot_anchor_id. ai_provider lets Private AI offer an external OpenAI-compatible provider: the kombify Wallet seals the item wallet_item_id (the provider's API key) to the node, which must be listed as a host target of that item, the node binds it to ai_provider_base_url, and a drift reconcile applies the setting. ai_provider_disable removes it. ssh_trust_recipient and ssh_trust_apply let the server trust the owner's kombify Wallet SSH CA: ssh_trust_recipient has the node answer the owner's recipient_challenge with its owner-signed recipient statement and returns it with the host target the owner lists on the CA item; the owner then asks the Wallet for the ssh-ca-trust delivery and ssh_trust_apply hands its sealed_delivery to the node, which installs TrustedUserCAKeys and the principals of each local user. Restore activation requires exactly one Idempotency-Key header, while other operations have no replay guarantee. Acceptance is not execution success; read the returned job and its scoped result to observe effects.

tools.name: start_workload_relocation
tools.title: Move workloads to another server
tools.description: Starts a verified move of workloads from the source server (this stack, `source_agent_id`) to a destination server of another owned stack. The workloads stop on the source while they transfer and the source is kept until both nodes verify the transfer; it can be resumed with the abort operation. Select either whole `projects` or individual `resource_uuids`. The transfer secret stays in Wallet custody (`wallet_item_id`) and domain switches go only to test domains. Needs exactly one Idempotency-Key; a replay returns the same job. Refused with 409 when a target holds locked services or server maintenance runs.

destination_agent_id.description: Guard agent of the destination server; must differ from the source.

items.description: OLD=NEW host names; NEW must be a test domain.

projects.description: Whole Coolify projects to move. Mutually exclusive with resource_uuids.

resource_uuids.description: Individual Coolify resources to move. Mutually exclusive with projects.

source_agent_id.description: Guard agent of the source server in this stack.

wallet_item_id.description: Wallet item id (itm_...) of the transfer secret; never the secret itself.

tools.name: stop_monthly_runtime
tools.title: Stop a managed server without destroying it
tools.description: Admits one generation-bound provider-control reconcile toward stopped. centron uses its graceful guest shutdown action; IONOS shuts the guest down over the execution channel because the IONOS provider stop releases the bound DHCP IPv4. The server keeps its disk, address, lease, capacity reservation and monthly billing.

power.description: Redacted ledger view of one generation-bound power reconcile. Stop and start keep the same resource generation, provider graph, bound IPv4, lease, capacity reservation and monthly billing; decommission is the only destroy. A pending status is accepted, not converged.

reconnect.description: What a reconnect did to recover the Guard session.

ssh_access.description: Node-verified outcome of the generation-bound owner SSH grant. Disable removes every owner-authorized key while keeping Kombify's execution channel; enable reinstalls the keys the owner authorized for this generation through the re-authenticated authorize-key route.

tools.name: sync_stack_identity
tools.title: Sync stack identity with Cloud
tools.description: Takes the kombify Cloud stack identity record (read by the caller through the Gateway with the user's own token; `null` when Cloud has none) and applies the sync rules to the local copy: adopt the Cloud record, confirm an identical one, or answer the body to push to Cloud with the `If-Match` revision. The call itself never writes to Cloud. When no local stack identity exists yet it only reports `homelab_missing`.

cloud.description: The Cloud record, or null when Cloud has no stack identity.

push.description: Present for `push_local`; the body to send to Cloud with `If-Match`.

tools.name: test_discovered_device_ssh
tools.title: Test SSH to a discovered device
tools.description: Opens one SSH connection with the login held in the Wallet item `ssh_wallet_item_id` (its key when it holds one, otherwise its password; a built-in wallet item must name this IP as its URL), resolved inside Techstack and never answered; nothing is stored. This contract accepts no password. A failed connection answers 200 with `success: false`. Non-admin callers may only test IPs from their own discovery results; admins may test arbitrary IPs. Local control planes only.

ssh_wallet_item_id.description: Wallet item holding the SSH key or password.

tools.name: test_remote_ssh
tools.title: Test remote SSH
tools.description: Opens one SSH connection to the given host with a credential held in the Wallet and reports whether it succeeded; nothing is stored. The credential is a Wallet node access item (`ssh_wallet_item_id`, bound to the host) or, on deployments that read the built-in wallet, the label of a stored SSH key. This contract accepts no password or private key. A failed connection answers 200 with `success: false` and the error. Requires the `native_v2_wizard` feature for the caller.

ssh_key_label.description: Label of a stored SSH key; only on deployments that read the built-in wallet.

ssh_wallet_item_id.description: Wallet node access item holding the SSH key or password.

tools.name: update_stack_identity_if_unchanged
tools.title: Update stack identity if unchanged
tools.description: Revision-checked variant of the stack identity update. `If-Match` carries the `local_revision` read from the stack identity, in double quotes (for example `"3"`); a stale revision answers 412 and a reused `Idempotency-Key` with different content answers 409. The edit is stored locally and marked pending until it is synced with kombify Cloud. The body is limited to 4096 bytes. Requires the Postgres control plane (503 `stack_identity_store_unavailable` otherwise).

if_match.description: Strong local revision in double quotes, for example `"3"`.

tools.name: update_wallet_item
tools.title: Update wallet item
tools.description: Merges the supplied fields into an item the caller owns and returns it redacted. Fields that are not supplied keep their value, including the stored secret and TOTP, which this contract can neither read nor change: the person sets those in the Wallet. The item kind and owner are immutable. An item owned by someone else answers 404. Only deployments that keep credentials in Techstack's own Wallet serve this route; elsewhere it answers 409 `self_hosted_only`.

notes.description: Free text; never put credentials here.

outputSchema.description:
Redacted wallet recovery item. `secret` and `totp` are never present in
list responses; only the `has_secret`/`has_totp` presence flags are
exposed. Additional metadata keys may be present.
